rounds.text: Meesho is demonstrating significant commercial momentum, evidenced by compounded sales growth of 40% over the trailing twelve months [E14] and a robust 30% over the last three years [E13]. This top-line expansion is increasingly efficient, as shown by the sharp improvement in quarterly operating margins from -15% to -6% in the most recent quarter [E20]. The company’s financial stability is anchored by a near-debt-free balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.01x [E26, E43]. Institutional confidence is surging, with foreign and domestic holdings increasing by a combined 13.85 percentage points since late 2025 [E31, E32], driving positive money flow [E33]. This institutional backing is reflected in the stock’s technical strength, as it maintains a relative-strength rating of 92 against the Nifty 500 and trades above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E36, E37]. Conceded: the company faces substantial headwinds from negative returns on equity [E12, E18], negative operating cash flow [E24, E25], and a high price-to-book valuation of 25.74x [E1, E45].

The valuation of Meesho Ltd is disconnected from its fundamental performance, as evidenced by a price-to-book ratio of 25.74x, which is significantly higher than the sector benchmark of 2.13x [E1, E6, E45]. This extreme premium is difficult to justify given that the company is currently destroying shareholder value, with a return on equity of -46.2% and a return on assets of -11.53% [E7, E12]. The business is currently burning cash, reporting negative operating cash flow of Rs -3,875 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -3,976 Cr as of March 2026 [E24, E25]. Furthermore, the company’s profitability remains unstable, with compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months at -20% and an inconsistent operating margin trend [E16, E21]. While the stock is trading near its 52-week high, the high annualised volatility of 55.1% suggests that investors are exposed to significant downside risk [E35, E39, E56]. Conceded: [E13, E14, E26, E31, E32, E33, E36, E37, E50, E51, E52, E53, E54].

Conceded: [E1, E6, E7, E12, E16, E21, E24, E25, E35, E39, E45, E56]. While the bear highlights rich valuation multiples and cash burn, these metrics ignore the powerful top-line momentum where compounded sales growth reached 30% over 3 years and accelerated to 40% over the trailing twelve months [E13, E14]. This revenue expansion significantly outpaces the sector median sales growth of 13.4%, proving that Meesho Ltd is capturing substantial market share in its space [E60]. The criticism regarding financial instability overlooks the pristine balance sheet where the company is almost debt free with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.01x and borrowings reduced to Rs 49 Cr [E26, E28, E43]. Furthermore, operating margins are inflecting positively, jumping 9 percentage points year-over-year in the September 2026 quarter [E20]. Smart institutional capital recognises this structural progress, driving positive money flow with foreign and domestic institutional holdings surging by a combined 9.11 percentage points [E31, E32, E33]. Finally, the market price reflects this underlying institutional conviction by trading strongly above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a stellar relative-strength rating of 92 [E36, E37].

Conceded: [E13, E14, E26, E28, E31, E32, E33, E36, E37, E43, E60]. While the bull highlights top-line growth, this revenue expansion is occurring alongside a deteriorating profitability profile, evidenced by a -20% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E16] and a median return on equity of -63% over the last three years [E17]. The claim of structural progress via margin improvement is undermined by the fact that the company’s operating margin remains negative at -8% [E19] and the yearly operating-margin trend is explicitly labeled as inconsistent [E21]. Furthermore, the bull’s reliance on institutional inflows ignores the fundamental reality that the company is burning cash, with negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -3,875 Cr and Rs -3,976 Cr respectively [E24, E25]. The valuation is disconnected from these operational losses, as the stock trades at a P/B of 25.74x [E1], which is vastly higher than the sector benchmark of 2.13x [E6]. Finally, the bull’s optimism regarding institutional conviction fails to address the risk of the low promoter holding of 16.34% [E30, E47], which suggests a lack of long-term alignment with the business's current trajectory.
